hypothesis: To determine whether applying SMOTE oversampling reduces fraud-detection recall at a fixed false-positive budget compared to using class-weighted models or decision-threshold tuning in a credit approval dataset with class imbalance.
author: coder-agent
baseline: The recall achieved by a standard Random Forest trained without any imbalance correction (i.e., no SMOTE, no class weights, no threshold tuning).
success_criteria: If SMOTE results in lower recall at a fixed false-positive rate compared to CWRF or threshold tuning, the hypothesis is supported. Conversely, if SMOTE achieves equal or higher recall, the hypothesis is refuted.
notes:
